text.p: Italian bonds and futures ended firm but off session highs after powering ahead in a market awaiting news on the country's key 1997 budget which the government is accelerating through parliament, traders said.
The December Btp Liffe contract earlier surged to a new record high of 126.70, above the previous high of 126.43 set a week ago today, but met resistance towards the end of trading.

"The Italian market is well set up and still has more room to rise but the weak tone of Bunds and T-Bonds is limiting the Btp futures," one trader said, adding the market traded in a narrow range of some 30 basis points.
The Dec Btp ended 32 bps up at 126.60.

Dealers said market feeling was that the December future could climb to above 128.00 before Christmas on expectations of falling interest rates. Also underpinning the market was sentiment the budet will be passed soon.
The U.S. market, which eased a touch after October production prices, does not expect a move from the FOMC meeting and is now looking to CPI data on Thursday.
"If The U.S. market rises tonight it's possible the Btp may touch 127.00 and 127.20 perhaps tomorrow," one trader said.
